races.name: Oddschecker Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner for Charlie Johnston with David Egan aboard; four wins from eight starts on good-to-firm-adjacent ground gives him a genuine fitness profile here, though a tendency to race prominently rather than truly lead means the style-fit flag is worth noting — he is in the right area but not an automatic banker.|
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on 107 and the one to beat, with two wins in his last five starts. A below-par seventh last time is the only recent blot, and he is proven over today's distance and going. The strong body of form makes him hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: Laureate Crown
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's lightly-raced 3yo has won two of his last three starts, both on good ground, and comes here off 22 days rest in fine heart; Oisin Murphy's hold-up approach suits a patient race on a track that rewards late runs, and the step to 1m2f after back-to-back 1m wins looks a natural progression.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though the run before that was a win, part of two victories from his last five starts. Laureate Crown has raced over today's going before and holds a solid second on our figures at 102, that latest run the obvious blot.

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's 3yo won consecutive races over 1m and 1m2f earlier this season and has solid Newmarket course form; the 38-day absence is a minor watch point but he schooled over this trip last time he was seen at his best, and he projects as the most natural tracker of Evanesco given his style and experience at this course.|
runners_data.comment: A below-par ninth last time out, 38 days ago, followed a third-placed effort the run before, part of two wins from his last five starts. Archers Bay has raced over today's distance and going before and can bounce back on our figures at 92.

runners_data.name: Decade Of Time
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's progressive 3yo arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and carries genuine form momentum, but his natural prominent style cannot be fully expressed here — he is likely to find himself covering more ground mid-pack than ideal, which tempers his claims despite the form.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and the run before that too, with a third the only blemish in his last three starts. Decade Of Time has raced over today's going before, though our figures are far more cautious than the official mark, at just 82.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: William Haggas supplies him in good heart and Tom Marquand is a strong booking, with four runs on good ground producing a win and two places; he would naturally race prominently but the crowded front end means he is likely to find himself tracking from a wider, deeper position than suits, and his 1m2f form is less proven.|
runners_data.comment: A strong threat on 101, well above his official 91. A win and a pair of placed efforts feature in his last five, and he is proven over today's distance and going. The one risk is a dip to fifth last time after a couple of quieter runs.

runners_data.name: Heraldry
runners_data.note: The longest absentee in the field at 67 days off, but John & Thady Gosden freshening horses rarely comes without purpose and William Buick's presence is significant; two of his three career starts show a win and a place, and his natural forward style compressed into midfield may actually suit a pace-collapse scenario where tactical speed wins the day.|
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our six on 78 and hard to fancy, back from a 67-day break. There is a little to like — runner-up last time out and a win earlier in a short recent sequence — but our figures leave him with plenty to find against these.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control tempo from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Newmarket. The pace is unlikely to be pressured early, meaning the race will be run at a controlled, even tempo that keeps the field compact through the middle stages before quickening from two furlongs out. Decade Of Time, Princling, and Heraldry are all natural prominent types who cannot all occupy those forward positions — Evanesco and Archers Bay are most likely to secure the prominent slots, with Decade Of Time, Princling, and Heraldry shuffled wider or deeper than ideal. A race run at a controlled, uncontested tempo on fast ground with a single pace-setter dictating terms heavily favours horses who can sit just behind the leader and sustain a finish — prominent-to-midfield closers with proven good-to-firm form are best positioned, while true hold-up horses face the challenge of a pace that may never fully test the front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Controls, Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco bowls along uncontested and the field cannot muster the sustained run to peg him back.
scenarios.body: Evanesco dictates at a comfortable, even tempo and, never put under pressure, finds extra when asked two furlongs out on ground that suits; horses pushed back from their natural prominent position lack the clean run they need to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Power Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is just fast enough to drain Evanesco's reserves and a closing burst materialises in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Laureate Crown, operating from hold-up, gets a perfect tow into the race and delivers a late challenge as Evanesco ties up; good-to-firm Newmarket suits Oisin Murphy's patient, late-delivering style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Archers Bay tracks Evanesco closely and the two fight out a sustained duel from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Archers Bay's course-and-distance form makes him the most dangerous stalker; a battle for the lead from the home turn tests Evanesco's stamina and opens the door for those just behind to mop up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early gallop creates a false-pace race and a sprint finish suits a fresh closer with tactical speed.
scenarios.body: Heraldry, freshest in the field at 67 days off and trained by Gosden with Buick up, could benefit from a dash-finish if the race falls asleep; Laureate Crown's two recent wins on similar ground also give him each-way claims in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Evanesco leads uncontested and never faces a challenge — if the pace is soft and David Egan switches off, the advantage of cover and a controlled tempo could render the field powerless to close.|

Archers Bay is the most likely horse to push Evanesco for the lead or sit directly behind him; if Marco Ghiani moves him up aggressively early, the dynamic changes materially and the pace lifts, benefiting closers.|

Decade Of Time, Princling, and Heraldry are all natural prominent types who will be competing for limited space behind Evanesco — any scrimmaging or traffic through the first half-mile could cost one or more of them a clear run when the race quickens.|

Laureate Crown's hold-up profile is the outlier in a field of prominent types — if the pace is genuinely even and the field strings out, Murphy will have the clearest run of all and arrives fresh enough to deliver a strong late effort.|

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for this race and every horse in the field has an OK going tag, but Heraldry's limited experience (three runs only) on fast ground means it is worth monitoring whether the conditions are at the sharp end of what he has encountered.|

races.name: Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes (Sponsored By Ultimate Provence) (Fillies' Group 2)

runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.note: Ran a solid second before winning over six furlongs on Good ground but faces a significant class jump into Group 2 company; her natural push forward will be squeezed by the volume of pace-committed fillies and she is likely to find herself in a spot not of her choosing.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time, 21 days ago, but she landed a win in her previous start to show ability. Proven over today's distance and going, our 92 rating keeps her in the mix, though a modest speed figure caps her claims from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.note: Won on debut over six furlongs at Goodwood on Good ground for the in-form Joseph O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle combination, arriving here fresh on nine days' rest with strong similar-going figures; a genuine prominent performer who should secure a clean position just off the lead.
runners_data.comment: Struck last time out just 9 days ago and returns quickly off the back of that, but sits bottom of these ratings on our figures. Alwaysanangel has run over today's distance before and wears a tongue-tie, though a modest speed figure leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Etonnante
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly landed her sole start on Good ground over six furlongs and returns after a 43-day break which is the longest layoff in the field; Clifford Lee takes the ride, and if fitness is spot on she has the tactical speed to sit behind Ruby Moon and pounce.
runners_data.comment: Won her latest outing but has not been seen since, a 43-day layoff now. Etonnante has raced over today's distance before, and while a 90 rating keeps her in the picture, second-bottom of our ratings makes her hard to trust fully fresh.

runners_data.name: Jolivette
runners_data.note: Bounced back with a win after a wide-margin debut defeat, both runs on Good over six furlongs for Andrew Balding and Colin Keane; she would ordinarily travel prominently but the crowded nature of the early order means she will likely find herself further back than ideal, tempering expectations.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is strong form and keeps her firmly in the picture, even after a below-par ninth last time out. Jolivette has raced over today's distance and going before, and a 96 figure marks her a live danger, though that latest run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Libertango
runners_data.note: Two wins from two starts over six furlongs on Good ground is the best unbeaten record in the field; George Boughey's filly is mapped to the rear purely because there are too many front-runners in this race, but she is no natural hold-up performer and Billy Loughnane will be keen to reclaim a forward berth early.
runners_data.comment: Unbeaten in her last two starts, most recently 21 days ago, and a top rating of 112 makes Libertango the one to beat on our figures. She has raced over today's distance and going before, with only the 21-day gap since her last outing worth a mention.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race, trained by Richard & Peter Fahey and ridden by Ryan Moore, she won her only start on Good ground and arrives with a clear positional advantage that Moore will exploit from the off; the lack of any serious challenger for the lead is her primary asset.
runners_data.comment: Won at the only start covered by this form line and returns in good order just 16 days later, making Ruby Moon a live threat to our selection. She has raced over today's distance and going before, though a modest speed figure is the one blot on an otherwise solid profile.

runners_data.name: Senorita Bonita
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Crisford-trained filly who won over five furlongs before finishing second stepping up to six; she wants to be involved early but the sheer number of forwardly-placed fillies means she is likely to find herself further off the pace than her form demands, adding risk to her chance.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a win in her prior start make her the chief danger to our selection, and a strong speed figure of 87 backs that up. Proven over today's distance and going, our 103 rating puts her right in this contest; she just needs a little more to close the gap.

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: Form reads 13 and 3 over six furlongs on Good ground for the lightly-resourced George Margarson yard, giving David Egan limited material to work with; her running style is unknown from a small sample, and she remains a significant unknown quantity at Group 2 level.
runners_data.comment: Just two recent starts to weigh — a third earlier and an unplaced effort last time. Proven over today's distance and going, our 91 rating and a fair speed figure keep her competitive, though she is yet to win and needs to bounce back.

races.paceDynamic: Ruby Moon is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight six. Alwaysanangel, Etonnante, and Libertango are all prominent-style fillies who will press forward behind her, but the field is saturated with pace-committed types — Acclamation Star, Jolivette, and Senorita Bonita are natural prominent racers who simply cannot all hold that position and will be shuffled into a midfield role they don't naturally seek. This compression of pace-hungry fillies behind a single uncontested leader creates a scenario where the early order is more contested in spirit than in practice, and the pace Ruby Moon sets is unlikely to be truly searching. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race close to the pace from the outset or sit just off the leader, travel fluently, and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a profile that benefits true prominent types and quick-finishing fillies who don't need a strong pace to be set.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ruby Moon Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby Moon leads at a controlled tempo and the prominent pack behind her cannot disrupt her rhythm, she dictates on her own terms.
scenarios.body: Ruby Moon has won her only start over six furlongs on Good ground and Ryan Moore will use the lack of competition up front to find the ideal position and conserve energy; a moderate, steady gallop compounds the advantage for the leader or those racing directly behind her in the first two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough that Ruby Moon ties up inside the final furlong and the fillies tracking her in second and third have more left.
scenarios.body: Alwaysanangel and Etonnante both won on Good ground over six furlongs and have the class and form to sustain a challenge in the final 100 yards if the leader has burned slightly more energy than comfortable; this shape rewards a strong staying-on finish from a filly who settled smoothly just off the early pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Pack Produces Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the bunching of redistributed prominent types creates a messy early order and a filly who finds clear air through the pack lands a blow.
scenarios.body: Senorita Bonita or Jolivette, though racing outside their natural position, could benefit if fractional interference unsettles the better-fancied fillies; this is a low-probability shape precisely because those fillies are not natural hold-up performers and the structured nature of a straight Newmarket six normally punishes positional disruption.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and Troublesome Guest, who showed improvement last time, cycles through on a muddled gallop.
scenarios.body: Troublesome Guest's form reads 3-0 over six furlongs on Good which is limited at this level, but an unusually stop-start tempo could scramble the form book; the unknowns around her style tag and light race record make this strictly a fringe scenario with minimal expectation of delivery.

watchPoints.text: Ruby Moon and Ryan Moore — if she gets an uncontested lead from the gates and sets a controlled tempo, the race may be over sooner than the price suggests.

Libertango — mapped to the rear only because of overcrowding at the front; watch where Billy Loughnane positions her in the first furlong, as reclaiming a prominent berth would significantly boost her chance.
Alwaysanangel and Etonnante — both unbeaten and roughly equal on ratings; whichever secures the cleaner passage directly behind Ruby Moon will likely have first run on the other in the final furlong.

Senorita Bonita and Jolivette — monitor how the early scramble for position affects them; if either is forced wide or checked in the first two furlongs, their challenge is likely compromised before the race has truly begun.
Troublesome Guest — her style tag is unknown and a single market move would significantly change how to read her role in the race; flag as a watch in the betting market pre-race.

races.name: Betway Trophy (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Roaring Legend
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, wearing a tongue-strap, and Colin Keane will look to exploit an uncontested lead; similar-going form is modest (no wins or places from five attempts), so its best chance is as a lead-through rather than winner, and its style-fit tag reflects it is racing slightly out of its true prominent comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: Our pick on his overall profile at 106, with a couple of runner-up efforts and a third earlier in his last five pointing to a capable sort, and he is proven over today's distance and going. He remains without a win of late and his last two starts have been quieter, but the underlying figures make the case.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Consistent Ian Williams stayer who has placed in competitive handicaps at this trip before, headgear (hood/tongue-strap) suggests he needs help switching off, and a return to good ground after soft-ground struggles is a clear positive; six sim-going runs with two wins and three places makes him a live contender if he can get a prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: A well-below-par eighth last time out followed an unplaced run before that, though a pair of runner-up efforts feature earlier in his last six starts. Beylerbeyi has raced over today's distance and going before and remains competitive on our figures at 99.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Ian Williams whose similar-going record is deeply unreassuring — 0 wins and just three places from 12 similar-going starts — and his last-time-out effort of 13th at this trip over good ground does nothing to inspire confidence; the Newmarket straight will test his finishing speed rather than his stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Modest reading to the bare form, with nothing better than a fourth in his last six starts. Real Dream has raced over today's distance and going before and tops our figures at 108, narrowly ahead of the next in line, with more upside than the results suggest.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over for Gosden, who has six winners from 48 runners in the 14-day window, and this four-year-old's form reads exceptionally well — two wins from six similar-going starts including a course win over 14f good ground; the step up to 1m6f for the first time is the only question, but his build-up of form strongly supports him as a leading player.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, though that followed a well-below-par sixth the run before, and the form in between has been mixed. Valedictory has raced over today's distance and going before, but sits down our list at 94 after a 48-day break.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's six-year-old landed a 12f good-ground contest recently and has strong course-distance form; David Egan takes over and the horse is just 13 days since his last run which won't be a concern at this age; suited by a prominent position and a steady pace at this trip, he could be dangerous if he gets a nice tracking role.|
runners_data.comment: A mid-pack contender on 95, quick to reappear just 13 days on. A win sits in the middle of his recent form, with placed efforts around it, though he was unplaced last time. Proven over today's distance and going, he has enough to be competitive without standing out.

runners_data.name: Goblet Of Fire
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's runner has won twice over this sort of trip on good ground and is a genuine front-runner by nature, but with more prominent types than the race can accommodate, Saffie Osborne is likely to find this horse shuffled back from its preferred position; style-fit and redistribution tags combine to make this harder to win than its form alone suggests, and a 68-day absence adds an extra uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, but that followed a well-below-par fifth the run before, and the form has been mixed. Goblet Of Fire has raced over today's distance and going before, though our figures rate him bottom of this field at 87, back from a 68-day absence.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this eight-year-old who is a natural hold-up horse with a good-ground course win over 12f on his record; his best recent effort was a 12f good-ground second, and while his tendency to finish from off the pace suits a quicker tempo, his form in the last three seasons has been unreliable and a repeat of his best is needed.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out marks a clear step forward from a fourth the run before, after modest form earlier this campaign. Majestic has raced over today's distance and going before and rates well above his official mark at 97, quick to reappear 13 days on.

runners_data.name: Wine Dark Sea
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's lightly-weighted four-year-old has won three of his last five and is clearly progressive, but he is a natural front-runner who will be unable to secure his preferred prominent position in this field — Lewis Edmunds will be riding against the horse's instincts from off the pace; the style-fit score of 0.91 reflects a real disadvantage in this specific race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and the run before that too, part of three wins from his last five starts, with a second and a sixth the only blips. Wine Dark Sea has raced over today's going before and sits mid-pack on our figures at 94.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Ian Williams fields three runners and this hold-up type has the weakest recent form of the trio — a string of mid-field and rear finishes across multiple surfaces — and Edward Greatrex on board will be hoping for a pace collapse that simply isn't likely with an uncontested front-runner setting a steady gallop; needs significant improvement on recent showings.|
runners_data.comment: The bare form reads poorly — a run of midfield-and-worse finishes, and winless in his last five. But our figures rate him well clear of that at 95, helped by a solid speed figure, and he is proven over today's distance and going. Whether he can run to our number is the question.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old is a genuine prominent racer who has finished 3rd and 4th in good-ground handicaps at this sort of trip, but Connor Beasley will find him unable to get his natural early position with rivals crowding that role; the redistribution to midfield means he faces an uphill task, and recent form includes three defeats, though the style-fit score of 0.92 is the highest of the redistributed group.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five and down among these on our figures at 93. He was unplaced last time, with a third his best recent effort further back. Proven over today's distance and going, but he needs to step up sharply to figure.

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Legend is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the early lead, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket. The pace will be honest but not scorching — a lone leader setting fractions to suit himself creates a race run to the benefit of those racing prominently or just off the pace, able to conserve energy before the Rowley Mile's long run-in. Goblet Of Fire, Pole Star, and Wine Dark Sea are all natural prominent types who will be squeezed back into midfield roles they would not naturally choose, reducing their ability to get competitive positions and making their task harder. The race shape overwhelmingly favours runners who can sit just behind the leader or in the first three, travel comfortably through a controlled pace, and then produce a sustained finish — making prominent-to-midfield closers with good Newmarket or stamina form the prime tactical profile to target.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend sets a genuine but unchallenged gallop and the race unfolds at a steady-to-honest tempo with no disruption.
scenarios.body: Roaring Legend dictates from the front without pressure, allowing Valedictory and Beylerbeyi to track comfortably in second and third, before the runners rounding the Dip produce a sustained stamina-based finish that rewards those who travelled fluently throughout. Prominent horses with proven good-ground form and stoutness over this trip are the direct beneficiaries of this controlled, front-runner-led shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves sufficiently steady that Roaring Legend, having controlled every yard, has enough in reserve to repel all challengers up the Rowley Mile straight.
scenarios.body: Keane on Roaring Legend engineers a false sense of security in the chasing pack, and the unchallenged fractions leave him with a decisive lead at the two-furlong pole that no hold-up horse can claw back in time. True stayers who can front-run with economy on fast ground are validated here, and the long Newmarket straight actually extends the leader's advantage rather than helping closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop proves quick enough through the middle stages that Roaring Legend is weakening late, and a runner held off the early pace produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Majestic, who holds natural hold-up form and recent good-ground credentials, or Asgard's Captain sweeping from midfield could benefit if the tempo lifts sufficiently in the back straight to open up the race for late finishers. This shape requires a genuinely honest pace rather than the slow-to-moderate gallop that a lone, uncontested front-runner is most likely to produce, making it a secondary possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Goblet Of Fire, Pole Star, or Wine Dark Sea break sharply and contest the lead with Roaring Legend, creating a genuinely contested, strong pace.
scenarios.body: Pressure on Roaring Legend from the outset would transform this into a truly run race, burning up the front two or three and handing the advantage to hold-up runners who have conserved their energy deep into the contest. However, given all three prominent types are carrying style-fit penalties and are likely to find themselves further back than ideal, this scenario depends on uncharacteristic tactical decisions from their jockeys and must be rated a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Valedictory — William Buick securing a prominent pitch behind Roaring Legend would be the most dangerous development in this race, given his two similar-going wins, strong course form, and first-time attempt at 1m6f for an in-form Gosden team.

Goblet Of Fire, Pole Star, and Wine Dark Sea — watch the first furlong to see whether any of these three redistributed prominent types break sharply and attempt to challenge Roaring Legend for the lead, which would fundamentally alter the pace shape of the race.

Asgard's Captain — David Egan is known for positive, front-foot riding, and if he tries to track Roaring Legend in second or third from flag-fall rather than racing further back, this six-year-old becomes significantly more dangerous given his recent 12f good-ground form.

Roaring Legend's similar-going record (0 wins, 0 places from five attempts) — if the pace becomes genuinely honest rather than truly slow, this horse's tendency to weaken late on fast ground could collapse the front end earlier than expected and open the race for closers from further back.

Beylerbeyi's headgear (hood and tongue-strap) — watch whether the combination allows him to settle comfortably in a prominent position early, as his 14f good-ground placed efforts suggest he needs a smooth, uninterrupted passage to produce his best work.

races.name: Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Falmouth Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 1)

runners_data.name: Balantina
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's 3yo has six runs on good/firm ground with a solid 1W3P return and won over this trip at Leopardstown in May; races prominently and should find a clean position here, though her recent form string (3251-5) is patchy and the step to Group 1 level is a stiff ask at OR=113.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, though the run before that was a win, with only the one success from her last five starts. She has raced over today's distance and going before, but our figures leave her towards the rear of this field at 108.

runners_data.name: Evolutionist
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 3yo has two wins and five places from seven starts on good ground and is in strong form, but she is a natural prominent racer whose chance is complicated by the crowded pace positions in this field — her true style cannot be expressed here if Precise and Balantina dominate the early stages, and that style-fit discount is real at STYLE_FIT=0.92.
runners_data.comment: A below-par eighth last time out came after a runner-up effort the run before, with a win also among her last five starts. Evolutionist has raced over today's distance and going before and rates a threat at 115, though her latest effort is the concern.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: The race's controlling influence — six wins from eight on good ground and an unbeaten record over this trip; Ryan Moore will jump her cleanly and set his own tempo, and an uncontested lead on fast Newmarket ground is a serious weapon, although her one poor run (7th in the Guineas) shows she is not infallible at this level.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and the run before that too, part of four wins from her last five starts, with only a seventh interrupting the sequence. Precise has raced over today's distance and going before and rates strongly at 120, a leading threat on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo won over 8f on good ground at Newbury and ran 2nd in the same conditions, giving her the going credentials, but she has been off 35 days, has no wins on softer variants she has encountered, and her natural tendency to race up with the pace is likely squeezed out in this field — the redistribution is the key caution against overstating her chance.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, but the run before last time's ninth was a much better third, so there's clearly ability there. Venetian Lace has raced over today's distance and going before and holds solid claims on our figures at 111.

runners_data.name: Venosa
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up type in this seven-runner field, trained by A P O'Brien and ridden by Wayne Lordan, but her record reads zero wins from six attempts on good/firm ground and she comes into this Group 1 off a 61-day break with an OR of just 89 — the pace shape and her own form make her a very long shot.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts, though the run before last time's below-par effort was a solid third. Venosa has raced over today's distance before, returning from a 61-day break, but sits bottom of this field on our figures at 84.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 4yo mare is the standout on recent form with five wins from six starts on good ground over 8f and carries the senior weight of 135lbs; Colin Keane's record in big-field prominent races is strong and her course-and-distance profile is exemplary — she is the horse whose profile fits this race shape most tightly.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in a row, the latest last time out, are part of three victories from her last five starts. Blue Bolt has raced over today's distance and going before, carries 135 lb from draw 5, and rates a leading threat on our figures at 122.

runners_data.name: Jancis
runners_data.note: The 5yo carries joint top-weight and has three wins and five places from eleven runs on good ground; Sean Levey will need to be aggressive to claim a prominent berth given the redistribution pressure, and while Jancis has the form to be competitive if she gets her position, the W McCreery yard is 0/17 in the past 14 days, adding a marginal caution.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, Jancis also has a win in her last five starts. She has raced over today's distance and going before, carries 135 lb from draw 1, and is our pick on that progressive profile at 122.

races.paceDynamic: Precise (Ryan Moore, A P O'Brien) is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner Group 1 and will dictate from the front on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's Rowley Mile — a track that genuinely rewards horses who can control from the front and quicken off a true gallop. With no rival likely to seriously pressurise her for the lead, she sets a sustainable, professional pace rather than a suicidal one, meaning she arrives at the Dip with petrol in the tank. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and close-tracking prominent profile: a controlled pace set by a quality lead horse on fast ground over a fair mile suits those who can settle just behind and pounce in the straight, rather than those forced to make up wide margins from deep off a moderate tempo. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all secure their natural position — Jancis, Evolutionist, and Venetian Lace are genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to land the spots they want, and of the three, Jancis (Sean Levey) has the form and jockey profile to be most aggressive in claiming a realistic tracking position, while Evolutionist and Venetian Lace are most at risk of racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Precise Dictates, Blue Bolt Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Precise sets a controlled lead and the pace holds true to Good to Firm standard, rewarding those who track close.
scenarios.body: Precise controls tempo from the front without pressure, setting a fair but not punishing gallop; Blue Bolt (Colin Keane), who has won five from six on good ground over this trip and is proven at tracking a strong lead, is ideally positioned to challenge deep into the Rowley Mile straight and overhaul her late. Horses with front-running or close-prominent profiles on fast ground at Newmarket benefit most here, and Blue Bolt's 4yo experience and OR=115 give her the class ceiling to convert.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, Balantina Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is just honest enough to string the field out and Balantina (Oisin Murphy) produces her best closing effort from a prominent position.
scenarios.body: Balantina has placed or won in similar going six from seven times and can race prominently for Donnacha O'Brien's yard; if the pace is true and she settles just off Blue Bolt, she has the class at OR=113 to sustain a strong run through the final two furlongs on the Rowley Mile's punishing straight. This shape suits a filly who can travel smoothly in second or third gear and deliver a clean finish rather than a sudden burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Backfires, Jancis Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Jancis (Sean Levey) manages to secure a prominent berth closer to the pace than her mapped position suggests and the race produces a one-run, front-to-back finish.
scenarios.body: Jancis has genuine prominent-running credentials — three wins and five places from eleven attempts on good ground — and if Levey is proactive enough to claim a position near the front early, she could prove the pace-map mapping was overly pessimistic. However, this scenario is discounted precisely because she is unlikely to get that position in this competitive field, meaning her chance depends on circumstances that may not materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Closers Denied
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or becomes falsely slow, gifting the front two a free rein to the line without any hold-up horse able to close.
scenarios.body: Venosa (Wayne Lordan, OR=89) is the only true hold-up type in this field but her record — zero wins from six on good ground and a string of poor finishes — makes her an unreliable beneficiary even if the pace does compress. A falsely slow race over a flat Newmarket mile would most likely play into Precise's stamina-conserving strengths rather than produce a dramatic late swoop from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Blue Bolt carries 135lbs as a 4yo in a fillies' and mares' Group 1 but her five wins from six on good ground over this exact trip make her the most dangerous horse in the race if she tracks Precise from the outset.

Jancis, Evolutionist, and Venetian Lace are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which of them, if any, manages to secure a realistic tracking berth behind Precise.

Precise's one blot — a 7th-place finish in the 1000 Guineas over this exact course and distance — means Ryan Moore will be under pressure to produce a more controlled, front-running performance than on that occasion; if she gets competitive early or is pushed wide, her pace advantage evaporates.

Venosa has been off 61 days and has not placed on good ground in six attempts; unless the race falls apart tactically and produces an unusually slow tempo, she is unlikely to land a blow from her hold-up position.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for the 3:35 — faster than the declared Good — which will compress sectional times and further reward horses with a clean prominent position over those forced to make up ground in the straight.

races.name: Weatherbys Banking Group British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: Tatterstall
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong similar-going record (12/15) on Good ground over five furlongs; Connor Beasley knows this horse well and Dods keeps a solid 14-day strike rate; 15 days since last run is ideal freshness and a placed effort last time out suggests he retains form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four runs this term but the form has held up, with a second last time out, 15 days ago, the pick of them. Tatterstall races over today's distance and going, and a stand-out 93 speed figure hints at more to come than his placings suggest.

runners_data.name: Rosario
runners_data.note: William Buick adds serious upside to a horse with a win and three places on similar going (12/15); has been consistent in defeat at this level and the five-furlong trip on Good to Firm is squarely in his wheelhouse, though OR=88 means he needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five runs this campaign but a whopping 94 speed figure marks him out as an underrated threat to our selection. Rosario has raced over today's distance and going before, with a fifth last time out, 18 days ago, forgivable given that clock form.

runners_data.name: Twilight Calls
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old who actually won over five furlongs on Good ground and has two places from five similar-going runs; the visor is retained, Saffie Osborne is an astute booking and Spencer's stable is in decent form (5/19 over 14 days) — worth noting this horse has genuine course-distance winning form.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on 100 and the one to beat, with a leading speed figure of 96. He was runner-up last time out and has a win to his name earlier in the sequence, and he is proven over today's distance and going. A patchier spell further back is the only caveat, but his best recent form sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Rapper's Delight
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent racer who has twice finished second over this distance on Good or similar ground; the visor is on, Spencer saddles a second runner here in a yard firing at 2/17 over 14 days, but only 3/8 similar-going runs have been placed and a run just five days ago warrants scrutiny.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five runs this term but a second last time out, just 5 days ago, shows him firmly in form and primed for a quick reappearance. Rapper's Delight wears a visor, has raced over today's distance before, and an 86 speed figure keeps him among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Never Just A Dream
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer whose natural style is to come from the rear; bumped to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers — Kent's yard is quiet (0/2, 14 days) and the 29-day absence, combined with a step back to five furlongs from a six-furlong habit in recent form, makes this a speculative profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts this campaign but a consistent yardstick of two fourths either side of blank efforts, and a strong 91 speed figure marks him a big danger to our selection. Never Just A Dream has raced over today's distance and going before, though a 29-day absence is the query.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a win over six furlongs on Standard and a previous placed effort, but the similar-going numbers on Good are poor (4/15, no wins or places) — a genuine closer by nature who will find it hard to secure a position deep enough to finish with purpose in a competitive 12-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back but the placings have since faded, a fifth last time out 13 days ago the most recent evidence. Star Chorus has raced over today's distance and going before, and though a fair 84 speed figure offers some hope, second-bottom of our ratings makes him a hard sell.

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Has the most compelling course-and-distance profile of any hold-up type in the race, with 13/15 similar-going runs producing three wins and four places over five furlongs on Good; Murphy is a positive booking but the horse is a true rear-of-field operator who needs a genuine pace and room to close, conditions not guaranteed today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five runs but has stayed competitive with a pair of fourths among those efforts, the latest a fifth 22 days ago. Rocking Ends races over today's distance and going, and a fair 87 speed figure keeps him in this midfield mix from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the race's pace anchor; Moore will dictate terms but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) acknowledges this is not a horse that comfortably leads at this level, and the 27-day layoff on Good ground with a modest 1W/2P from eight similar-going runs suggests vulnerability to a sustained challenge in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five runs this term but largely competitive, a second the standout among mostly top-five efforts. Our Cody has raced over today's distance and going before, and a strong 90 speed figure hints she has more to offer, though it is 27 days since that run.

runners_data.name: Emperor Spirit
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish; a true hold-up type pushed into the midfield map position by the crowded rear, and the combination of the fading flag, recent run just seven days ago and only 1W/3P from nine similar-going runs makes his claims limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five and hard to fancy on 87, down the field on our figures. He was runner-up last time out, just 7 days ago, so he arrives fresh, and he is proven over today's distance and going. But the in-and-out nature of his form leaves him needing more against these.

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who showed a win over six furlongs on Good going but has produced a string of disappointing efforts since; flags a tendency to fade in the finish, the apprentice claim from Kyle McHugh (7lbs) is the main positive, and the drop to five furlongs from a six-furlong background is an open question.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy at 82 and 10th of 12 on our figures. A win sits at the start of this recent run, but the form has slipped badly since — well beaten in each start and unplaced last time. Proven over today's distance and going, but the yard is cold (1/29, 3%) and he needs a big turnaround.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Prominent-style six-year-old for Robert Cowell who wears a hood and has been consistently placed in Good-ground sprints (7/15, 1W/4P); Billy Loughnane partners a horse who naturally tracks the pace, and this race shape — where he can sit just behind Our Cody — suits his profile well.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts this term but has stayed competitive, a pair of thirds the highlights either side of a blank effort. Rhythm N Hooves wears cheekpieces, has raced over today's distance and going before, and a strong 91 speed figure keeps him firmly involved from stall 3.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying the minimum weight (121lbs) with a wide draw likely in a large field; has a win on Soft going and some placed efforts but similar-going numbers on Good are modest (4/14) and the trainer (Lemos De Souza) has a quiet 14-day record (0/8) — the lightweight angle is the main interest.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has since found only minor money, a fifth last time out 35 days ago his most recent form. U S S Charleston has raced over today's distance and going before, and though a fair 82 speed figure offers a shred of hope, he anchors these ratings on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Our Cody is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Ryan Moore in the saddle, is likely to be allowed to stride on and control matters from the outset at a sustainable, metronomic gallop rather than a suicidal split — this is Good to Firm ground over five furlongs at Newmarket, so the tempo will be honest but not extreme. Behind him, Rapper's Delight, Rhythm N Hooves and U S S Charleston will seek prominent positions, though in a 12-runner sprint field they cannot all settle where they want, meaning early jostling for the favoured stands-side position is probable. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Star Chorus, Rocking Ends, Never Just A Dream and Emperor Spirit are genuine closers but are mapped to midfield because true rear-of-field positions will be difficult to find in this competitive sprint; their redistributed placement tempers their winning likelihood in a shape that requires a clean late run. With a single honest pace-setter setting a controlled tempo and no genuine pace battle to stretch the field, this race shape favours horses with tactical versatility — those able to race in the first half of the field and sustain their effort to the line — over pure hold-up finishers who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Our Cody Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Our Cody is allowed to roll along uncontested and the field settles into a tidy, organised shape behind him.
scenarios.body: Moore dictates from the front at a fair but manageable tempo, denying the closers the strong pace injection they need to close; horses racing prominently in his wake are best placed to pick up the pieces if he weakens. Rapper's Delight and Rhythm N Hooves, both tracking the leader in natural positions, are the primary beneficiaries, with Tatterstall and Twilight Calls able to make ground from slightly further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the prominent runners tie up in the final furlong, allowing genuine hold-up horses to get through.
scenarios.body: Rocking Ends has outstanding similar-going form (13/15) over this exact trip at Newmarket and, if he can find a clear run from midfield, his course-and-distance profile is the most compelling in the field. Tatterstall and Twilight Calls, both with strong form on Good ground over five furlongs, have the sectional speed to finish strongly if gaps materialise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Rank Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Rapper's Delight, Rhythm N Hooves and U S S Charleston all push up to challenge Our Cody, creating a contested pace that fractures the field.
scenarios.body: A genuine multi-horse battle for the lead would produce a stronger gallop and set the race up for those sitting just off the pace; horses with the ability to race prominently without leading, then sustain their effort, will be rewarded. Our Cody and Rapper's Delight, both with STYLE_FIT flags, may suffer for the early exertion, opening the door for Twilight Calls and Rosario to close with purpose.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Our Cody gets very easy fractions early and the field bunches, triggering a mass sprint finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race turning into a flat-out dash favours horses with raw speed and low weight; U S S Charleston (121lbs, OR=78) carries the lightest weight in the field and could benefit from a messy, speed-off finale. Rhythm N Hooves, a proven front-rank type on Good ground, could also pick up prize money if the field fans wide and racing luck plays a role.

watchPoints.text: Our Cody's early position is critical — if Rapper's Delight, Rhythm N Hooves or U S S Charleston push to dispute the lead, the race shape changes entirely and the controlled-tempo scenario collapses.

Rocking Ends is a high-class closer on this going and trip (3W/4P from 13 similar-going runs) but is mapped to midfield out of natural position — watch whether Oisin Murphy can find a route through in the final furlong, as a clear run could make him dangerous.

Tatterstall and Twilight Calls both carry strong similar-going form and are in natural running positions for this race shape; if the pace is honest, both are capable of finishing with purpose and either could steal a place without being the obvious market fancy.

The stands-rail draw will be critical over Newmarket's five furlongs — horses that secure an early stands-side position in the first two furlongs will have a significant structural advantage, and crowding in a 12-runner field could compromise the chance of any horse slow to break.

Emperor Spirit and Underwriter are both flagged as horses that fade in the finish — if either is prominent in the early stages, their tendency to weaken is worth monitoring as a pointer to the winning margin and which closers are eating into the field late.

races.name: Jockey Club Estates Handicap

runners_data.name: Flight Control
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good at Newmarket most recently and has finished in the frame on all four starts at this track; William Pyle's booking is modest but this horse's course-and-distance profile is the most relevant in the field and she should secure a forward pitch without needing to fight for it.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a strong danger to our selection on 85. A win features earlier in his last four, and he is proven over today's distance and going. The placed-but-not-winning efforts since that win are the minor query, but he is firmly involved.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners a horse that ideally wants to race up with the pace, but with so many prominent types in this field she is likely to find herself covering more ground than ideal mid-division; Ian Williams is in good recent form (5/28 T14) though the gelding's 16th of 19 in a 7f handicap here last time is a concern at this course.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out, 16 days ago, kept the form ticking over after a win four starts back, and Aqua Bear rates a solid danger to our selection on that book. He has raced over today's distance and going before, though an unplaced effort somewhere in that sequence is the one blemish.

runners_data.name: Calling A Star
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over for Richard Hughes and brings serious jockey quality, but this filly naturally wants to race prominently and will find the traffic heavier than she would like given how many rivals share her style; her last win came at 6f on Good so the step up to 7f on similar ground is not guaranteed to suit her finishing action.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, 25 days ago, to confirm a level of ability that has produced two wins from her last five starts, though the form either side has been mixed. Calling A Star has raced over today's distance and going before, and with the yard managing just a 5% strike lately, the signals are mixed too.

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking lifts the profile of a horse who has placed three times from five starts on Good ground, winning over this exact 7f trip at Newmarket last time out — the form is rock solid; forced back from his natural position by the crowded prominent section, Murphy's experience may allow him to find a better spot than his raw style suggests.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, 20 days ago, and a gap between that form and his modest 75 official mark makes Toastmaster a serious threat to our selection. He has raced over today's distance and going before, with a run of consistent minor-money finishes in support, though he must confirm that improvement.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly has been consistent without winning, placing twice in five runs, and her Newmarket 7f form (third and second from two tries) is respectable; George Wood inherits a horse who will struggle to get her preferred prominent pitch with this much pace in the race, softening her already modest winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five runs this term, though a third last time out, 14 days ago, followed a runner-up effort and shows him capable of going close. Kimbara has raced over today's distance and going before, but a rating of 75 leaves him with more to find near the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Lion of Mali
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has won twice over 7f on Good at Newmarket in his last five starts — the course-and-distance record is the strongest in the field — and David Egan is a class jockey booking; another horse pushed back from his preferred prominent berth, though his raw ability on this track means he retains serious claims if he can access a position just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Four wins from his last six starts, including the latest 28 days ago, mark Lion Of Mali out as a fair yardstick even from a modest 72 official mark. He has raced over today's distance and going before, though a lengthy absence since that win is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride for an Irish raider trained by D Donovan, a stable with no entries in the T14 window; the hold-up style is genuinely suited to a compressed finish, and she has won on Good ground over further than this, though the step down to 7f from her recent 8f-9f starts is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but the placings have since faded, a sixth last time out 14 days ago the most recent evidence. Daretobedifferent has raced over today's distance and going before, and while a modest 73 rating leaves her fighting for minor honours, she has been running consistently enough in defeat.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners a horse who wears headgear and has yet to win, with a best recent finish of third over 8f on Good; the hold-up style is authentic but the form profile — no win from seven starts and an OR of just 59 — makes it hard to see her troubling the judge even in a scenario that perfectly suits closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five runs and races in a hood, with a third the highlight of a string of modest efforts, the latest a fifth 15 days ago. Ice Cube has raced over today's distance and going before, but bottom of our ratings makes him hard to fancy in this field.

runners_data.name: Three Non Blondes
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners the field's lone confirmed front-runner for a trainer (Hayley Burton) who has had a quiet fortnight; the top-rated runner at OR 82 and a course winner over 7f on Standard going, she is the key pace-setter and her ability to control tempo uncontested gives her a structural advantage even if her style-fit score suggests some discount when she races in an atypical role.
runners_data.comment: Two wins from her last five starts, including a fine placed effort last time out, underpin the claims of our top-rated selection here. Three Non Blondes has raced over today's distance and going before, and an 88 rating heads this field, with the 20-day break since her last run the only note of caution.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking for Ed Dunlop immediately elevates this horse's prospects — Moore rarely gets on horses without a live chance — and Sierra Sands has two wins from seven starts on Good ground at 6f-7f at Newmarket; a natural prominent racer who should get her position without fighting for it, making her one of the best-placed horses in the field structurally.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, 15 days ago, backing up an earlier success with a game display, though the form in between was patchier. Sierra Sands has raced over today's distance and going before, and a fair rating of 82 keeps him competitive, despite a modest speed figure.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has a strong T14 record (6/45) and Edward Greatrex rides a filly whose last five runs are all at 6f with no Newmarket win yet; the step up to 7f on Good to Firm may not be an obvious positive but her form shows consistent placing at the shorter trip, and she may find the extra furlong drawing out a better performance.
runners_data.comment: A couple of runner-up efforts and a win feature earlier in his last four, but he could only manage a below-par fourth last time. Proven over today's distance and going, our 82 rating keeps him fairly in the mix here.

races.paceDynamic: Three Non Blondes is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press her on the front end, she is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the Rowley Mile's seven-furlong start down to the Dip. That measured tempo will compress the race, keeping the field relatively bunched into the closing stages and making the finish a sharp tactical test rather than a stamina grind. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Aqua Bear, Calling A Star, Toastmaster, Kimbara and Lion of Mali are all natural prominent racers who will be forced to race deeper than their optimum, with Sierra Sands and Flight Control the most likely to actually secure a forward berth behind Three Non Blondes given their form profile and jockey booking quality. A controlled pace with a select few horses in the right positions favours those who can travel prominently in the slipstream of the leader and produce a decisive finishing kick from two furlongs out — horses with tactical speed, good Newmarket form on Good to Firm, and jockeys confident enough to commit early will have a clear structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Three Non Blondes sets a steady tempo unchallenged and the horses who successfully hold a forward position produce the best turn of foot.
scenarios.body: Three Non Blondes dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, and by the time the field straightens for home the race becomes a sprint for those sitting two or three lengths off the pace; the compressed finish rewards those with a sharp, powerful finishing kick from a close-up position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Three Non Blondes gets an uncontested lead and the steady tempo proves just slow enough that she conserves energy to repel challenges in the Dip.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to go with her early, Three Non Blondes essentially time-trials the field and still has reserves when the challengers arrive at the two-furlong pole; the Good to Firm ground aids her stride and Ryan Moore's rivals may leave their runs fractionally too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected — perhaps Flight Control or Sierra Sands push up aggressively — and creates enough of a genuine gallop for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace with multiple horses committed forward burns fuel in the first half, and Daretobedifferent or Lion of Mali, tucked in and waiting, get the cleaner, faster finish they need to reel in tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and bunches so tightly that hold-up horses cannot find daylight, turning the finish into a sprint where the true closers are inconvenienced rather than aided.
scenarios.body: Ice Cube and Daretobedifferent, natural hold-up types, remain trapped in traffic as the field concertinas; however if a gap opens late Daretobedifferent's proven finishing ability on Good ground gives her the best chance of any closer.

watchPoints.text: Sierra Sands and Three Non Blondes are the two highest-rated runners and are set to occupy the front two positions — watch whether Ryan Moore allows Sierra Sands to sit just behind the leader or pushes up to challenge for the front, as that decision will define the pace shape entirely.

Lion of Mali has the strongest course-and-distance form in the field (two wins over 7f on Good at Newmarket) but will be forced to race further back than his natural style demands — watch whether David Egan can manoeuvre him into a forward position in the first furlong before the field settles.

Toastmaster is a Newmarket 7f winner with Oisin Murphy booked, and though he is redistibuted into midfield by the race shape, Murphy's tactical intelligence means he could steal a march on rivals who are slower to react at the start — watch his position at the two-furlong marker.

Calling A Star with William Buick is the most interesting jockey upgrade in the race; if Buick can place her in the one or two spots immediately behind Three Non Blondes rather than becoming buried mid-pack, her speed figure on Good ground makes her a genuine threat in a scenario that rewards prominent runners.

Daretobedifferent's Irish raider angle and authentic hold-up style make her worth monitoring in-running — if the pace does compress the field and a gap opens in the straight, her Good-ground form over 7f-8f suggests she will be staying on at the finish when others are tying up.
